\label{lemma-essential}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A \subset B$ and $B \subset C$ are essential extensions, then
$A \subset C$ is an essential extension.
\item If $A \subset B$ is an essential extension and $C \subset B$
is a subobject, then $A \cap C \subset C$ is an essential extension.
\item If $A \to B$ and $B \to C$ are essential surjections, then
$A \to C$ is an essential surjection.
\item Given an essential surjection $f : A \to B$ and a surjection
$A \to C$ with kernel $K$, the morphism $C \to B/f(K)$ is an essential
surjection.
\end{enumerate}
statement: In an abelian category, a monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$ is *essential* if every nonzero subobject of $B$ meets $A$ nontrivially; an epimorphism $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ is *essential* if no proper subobject of $A$ maps onto $B$. Then: (1) essential injections $A\hookrightarrow B\hookrightarrow C$ compose to an essential injection $A\hookrightarrow C$; (2) if $A\hookrightarrow B$ essential and $C\hookrightarrow B$, then $A\cap C\hookrightarrow C$ essential; (3) essential surjections $A\twoheadrightarrow B\twoheadrightarrow C$ compose to an essential surjection; (4) if $f:A\twoheadrightarrow B$ essential and $q:A\twoheadrightarrow C=A/K$, the induced $C\to B/f(K)$ is an essential surjection.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-hull-unique}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$, $N$ be $R$-modules and let $M \to E$
and $N \to E'$ be injective hulls. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for any $R$-module map $\varphi : M \to N$ there exists an
$R$-module map $\psi : E \to E'$ such that
$$
\xymatrix{
M \ar[r] \ar[d]_\varphi & E \ar[d]^\psi \\
N \ar[r] & E'
}
$$
commutes,
\item if $\varphi$ is injective, then $\psi$ is injective,
\item if $\varphi$ is an essential injection, then $\psi$ is an isomorphism,
\item if $\varphi$ is an isomorphism, then $\psi$ is an isomorphism,
\item if $M \to I$ is an embedding of $M$ into an injective $R$-module,
then there is an isomorphism $I \cong E \oplus I'$ compatible with
the embeddings of $M$,
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the injective hull $E$ of $M$ is unique up to isomorphism.
statement: An $R$-module $E$ is *injective* if every map to $E$ from a submodule extends across its ambient module. An *injective hull* of $M$ is an essential embedding $M\hookrightarrow E$ into an injective module. Let $M\hookrightarrow E$ and $N\hookrightarrow E'$ be injective hulls. (1) Every map $\varphi:M\to N$ has an extension $\psi:E\to E'$ commuting with the hull embeddings (not necessarily unique). (2) If $\varphi$ is injective, $\psi$ is injective. (3) If $\varphi$ is an essential injection, $\psi$ is an isomorphism. (4) In particular this holds when $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. (5) If $M\hookrightarrow I$ embeds into any injective $R$-module, then $I\simeq E\oplus I'$ with the specified $M$ embedding landing in the $E$ summand. Hence injective hulls are isomorphic over their embedded modules.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-indecomposable-injective}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $E$ be an indecomposable injective $R$-module.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is the injective hull of any nonzero submodule of $E$,
\item the intersection of any two nonzero submodules of $E$ is nonzero,
\item $\text{End}_R(E)$ is a noncommutative local ring with maximal
ideal those $\varphi : E \to E$ whose kernel is nonzero, and
\item the set of zerodivisors on $E$ is a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$
and $E$ is an injective $R_\mathfrak p$-module.
\end{enumerate}
statement: An $R$-module $E$ is *injective* if every map to $E$ from a submodule extends across its ambient module. An *injective hull* of $M$ is an essential embedding $M\hookrightarrow E$ into an injective module. An $R$-module is *indecomposable* if it is nonzero and has no decomposition as a direct sum of two nonzero modules. Let $E$ be an indecomposable injective $R$-module. (1) $E$ is an injective hull of every nonzero submodule. (2) Any two nonzero submodules of $E$ intersect nontrivially. (3) The possibly noncommutative ring $\operatorname{End}_R(E)$ is local, its unique maximal ideal consisting of endomorphisms with nonzero kernel. (4) The set $\mathfrak p=\{r\in R:\exists\,0\ne e\in E,\ re=0\}$ is prime and $E$ is injective over $R_{\mathfrak p}$, with its induced scalar structure.

\label{lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint}

$$

(A \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} A_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} A_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}}
\to \ldots \to A_{f_1\ldots f_r}) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} K
$$
functorially in $K \in D(A)$.

R\Hom_A(K, L) \longrightarrow R\Hom_B(K \otimes_A B, L \otimes_A B)

$$

\label{lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I = (f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ be an ideal
of $A$. Set $Z = V(I) \subset \Spec(A)$. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$
R\Gamma_I(A) \to
(A \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} A_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} A_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to
\ldots \to A_{f_1\ldots f_r}) \to R\Gamma_Z(A)
$$
in $D(A)$. If $M$ is an $A$-module, then we have similarly
$$
R\Gamma_I(M) \cong
(M \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} M_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} M_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to
\ldots \to M_{f_1\ldots f_r}) \cong R\Gamma_Z(M)
$$
in $D(A)$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-depth}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal, and
let $M$ be a finite $A$-module such that $IM \not = M$. Then
the following integers are equal:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{depth}_I(M)$,
\item the smallest integer $i$ such that $\Ext_A^i(A/I, M)$
is nonzero, and
\item the smallest integer $i$ such that $H^i_I(M)$ is nonzero.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we have $\Ext^i_A(N, M) = 0$ for $i < \text{depth}_I(M)$
for any finite $A$-module $N$ annihilated by a power of $I$.
statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, ideal $I$ and finitely generated $A$-module $M$, define $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ to be the maximal length of an $M$-regular sequence of elements of $I$ (and $\infty$ by convention if $IM=M$). A sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ is $M$-regular if each $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})M$ and the final quotient is nonzero. Assume $IM\ne M$, so $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ is finite. Then the following three integers are equal:
\[
\operatorname{depth}_I(M)
=\min\{i\ge0:\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(A/I,M)\ne0\}
=\min\{i\ge0:H_I^i(M)\ne0\},
\]
where $H_I^i(M)$ is the cohomology of the derived $I$-power-torsion functor (equivalently Čech local cohomology since $A$ is Noetherian). Moreover if $N$ is any finite module with $I^nN=0$ for some $n$, then $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(N,M)=0$ for every $i<\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$.

\label{lemma-depth-in-ses}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $0 \to N' \to N \to N'' \to 0$
be a short exact sequence of finite $A$-modules.
Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\text{depth}_I(N) \geq \min\{\text{depth}_I(N'), \text{depth}_I(N'')\}$
\item
$\text{depth}_I(N'') \geq \min\{\text{depth}_I(N), \text{depth}_I(N') - 1\}$
\item
$\text{depth}_I(N') \geq \min\{\text{depth}_I(N), \text{depth}_I(N'') + 1\}$
\end{enumerate}

For a Noetherian ring $A$, ideal $I$ and finitely generated $A$-module $M$, define $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ to be the maximal length of an $M$-regular sequence of elements of $I$ (and $\infty$ by convention if $IM=M$). A sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ is $M$-regular if each $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})M$ and the final quotient is nonzero. For a short exact sequence $0\to N'\to N\to N''\to0$ of *finite* $A$-modules and ideal $I$, put $d'=\operatorname{depth}_I(N')$, $d=\operatorname{depth}_I(N)$, $d''=\operatorname{depth}_I(N'')$ (using $\infty$ when $IN=N$). Then
$d\ge\min(d',d'')$,
$d''\ge\min(d,d'-1)$, and
$d'\ge\min(d,d''+1)$.
The inequalities are the depth lemma for this exact sequence.

\label{lemma-completion-local}
Let $I$ and $J$ be ideals in a Noetherian ring $A$. Let $M$ be a finite
$A$-module. Set $Z =V(J)$. Consider the derived $I$-adic completion
$R\Gamma_Z(M)^\wedge$ of local cohomology. Then
\begin{enumerate}

$$
0 \to R^1\lim H^{i - 1}_Z(M/I^nM) \to H^i(R\Gamma_Z(M)^\wedge) \to
\lim H^i_Z(M/I^nM) \to 0
$$
\end{enumerate}
In particular $R\Gamma_Z(M)^\wedge$ has vanishing cohomology
in negative degrees.

\label{lemma-composition-right-adjoints}
Let $A \to B \to C$ be ring maps. Then
$R\Hom(C, -) \circ R\Hom(B, -) : D(A) \to D(C)$
is the functor $R\Hom(C, -) : D(A) \to D(C)$.
statement:
For a homomorphism of commutative rings $\varphi:A\to B$, let $\varphi_*:D(B)\to D(A)$ be restriction of scalars. Its right adjoint $\mathcal C_\varphi(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,K)\in D(B)$ gives $B$ its action through precomposition on the $B$-argument. Then the canonical natural transformation
\[
\mathcal C_{C/B}\circ\mathcal C_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_{C/A}
\]
is an isomorphism; both sides are right adjoint to the same composite scalar restriction $D(C)\to D(A)$. This is an isomorphism of functors, not an untyped equality of two uses of $R\operatorname{Hom}$.
